item.title: Role of E-F Coupling on Low-latitude Ingression of Mid-latitude MSTIDs over the Indian Subcontinent
item.description: arXiv:2611.09310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study provides the first observational evidence that E-F region electrodynamic coupling regulates the southernmost latitudinal extent of nighttime mid-latitude medium-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances (MSTIDs) over the Indian subcontinent. We have analyzed multiple MSTID events using total electron content (TEC) measurements from a dense network of dual-frequency GNSS receivers across India, GNSS radio occultation (RO) profiles, and ionosonde observations from New Delhi during May-July 2025, a high solar activity period. The lowest geographic latitude, at which MSTIDs wavefronts reached, varied between 17{\deg}N and 25{\deg}N. Their low-latitude extension showed no significant correlation with background TEC, but was positively correlated with the geomagnetically mapped southernmost latitude of sporadic-E (Es) layers identified from GNSS-RO measurements. These events occurred during high solar activity, when F-region MSTID growth is generally suppressed. Therefore, our results suggest that electrodynamic coupling with the underlying Es-layers is essential for sustaining MSTIDs and enabling their low-latitude penetration during solar maxima.
item.dc:creator: Jeevan Upadhyaya, Dipjyoti Patgiri, Mehta Harsh Jayeshkumar, Rahul Rathi, Virendra Yadav, Satarupa Chakrabarti, Arun K. Upadhayaya, Sumanta Sarkhel

item.title: Successive Decimetric Bursts Associated with Breakout Magnetic Reconnection during the Decay Phase of an M-Class Flare
item.description: arXiv:2611.09332v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radio imaging spectroscopy diagnoses coronal electron acceleration and propagation by tracking energetic electron beams and locating energy-release sites. Using MUSER (0.4-2 GHz) and SDO data, we investigate decimetric radio emission during an eruption with an M1.1 flare on 17 December 2014. The eruption involves a twisted coronal structure evolving through three stages: a violent internal eruption, a rise-and-expansion phase, and a breakout eruption. The flare peaks at 01:50 UT during the internal eruption, while the cluster of successive type III-like decimetric bursts occurs in the decay phase, linked to the breakout eruption. The radio source coincides with a high-squashing-factor Q region from nonlinear force-free field (NLFFF) extrapolations, indicating a quasi-separatrix layer (QSL). We interpret the radio emission as consistent with plasma emission driven by nonthermal electrons accelerated by breakout reconnection at this QSL, between the outer envelope of the erupting structure and the surrounding corona. The successive bursts occur in the decay phase because breakout reconnection involves a larger, more energetic twisted structure at higher altitude, where an extended high-Q region, favorable acceleration geometry, and repeated sub-eruptions sustain efficient electron acceleration. Missing soft X-ray enhancement suggests most accelerated electrons escape upward or lose energy before reaching the chromosphere. The concentrated source positions of the successive radio bursts suggest pseudostreamers may act as particle accelerators, trapping electrons and directing them along a narrow layer. These results establish decimetric radio imaging as a powerful diagnostic of breakout reconnection and particle acceleration in the solar corona, with implications for energy release in pseudostreamer environments.
item.dc:creator: Suli Ma, Yihua Yan, Wei Wang, Hamish Reid, Ting Li, Xiaoshuai Zhu, Huadong Chen, Zhichao Zhou, Jing Huang, Linjie Chen, Chengming Tan, Xingyao Chen, Minghui Zhang, Xin Yao

item.title: Different exact-law formulations to calculate the energy cascade rate in magnetohydrodynamic turbulence with and without mean magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.09437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: At scales much larger than the ion inertial length and ion-gyroscale, space-plasma turbulence is often described within the framework of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). Using high-resolution direct numerical simulations with $1024^3$ grid points, we perform the first systematic numerical comparison of three exact-law formulations for the total energy cascade in homogeneous, but not necessarily isotropic, MHD turbulence: the Yaglom-Monin (YM), Banerjee-Galtier (BG), and two-point correlator formulations. Despite directional variations, the angle-averaged energy transfer rates for all three formulations show excellent agreement for zero, moderate, and strong background magnetic fields. These results clearly suggest the usefulness of alternative BG and correlator formulations for estimating the energy cascade rates in turbulent space plasmas when the required spatial derivatives are accessible through multi-spacecraft measurements. We also argue that the isotropic Politano-Pouquet (PP) formulation does not provide a true directional transfer rate and therefore its application as a single-direction energy transfer rate estimator leads to inaccurate values, especially under anisotropic conditions. Decomposing the exact formulations into RMHD and non-RMHD contributions, we also show that the RMHD cascade rates cannot be obtained merely by increasing the strength of the mean magnetic field in incompressible magnetohydrodynamic turbulence. Finally, a term-by-term analysis of different formulations reveals how different nonlinear interaction channels coexist and collaborate with each other to maintain the same energy cascade rate across the inertial scales.
item.dc:creator: Ramesh Sasmal, Supratik Banerjee

item.title: Solar Wind Classifications at Mars using Machine Learning Techniques
item.description: arXiv:2604.08710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding solar wind variability throughout the heliosphere is essential for fundamental space physics and future exploration of the Moon and Mars. The Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN (MAVEN) spacecraft has provided upstream solar wind measurements at Mars spanning Solar Cycles 24 and 25, enabling a statistical investigation of solar wind regimes at this heliocentric distance. In this work, we apply an unsupervised machine-learning framework combining Principal Component Analysis and K-Means clustering to a normalized, multi-dimensional solar wind dataset to identify recurrent solar wind regimes in a physically interpretable, data-driven manner. The resulting classification reveals distinct slow, fast, intermediate, and compressed solar wind regimes whose relative occurrence and temporal organization are strongly modulated by solar activity. This manuscript is part of the Heliophysics Summer School Machine Learning Special Collection.
item.dc:creator: Silvia Ferro, Catherine E. Regan, Austin M. Smith, Alvin J. G. Angeles, Nicholas A. Gross, Farzad Kamalabadi, Marco Velli, Jasper S. Halekas

item.title: The Baryon Budget of Galaxies across the First Billion Years
item.description: arXiv:2603.00230v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a complete census of the baryons in early galaxies to investigate the phases in which gas and stars reside, their corresponding budgets, depletion times, and stellar return fraction as a function of redshift and stellar age. We use the ColdSIM hydrodynamical time-dependent non-equilibrium chemistry simulations and perform a detailed analysis of the cold, warm, hot, and stellar phases for both bound structures (galaxies/CGM) and the diffuse IGM. We investigate in depth the cold HI and H2 components, explicitly computed in our simulations, and their relations with host mass, SFR, metallicity and depletion times. We also provide observational insights and discuss the implications for stellar mass functions, PopIII star formation and changes in the IMF. We find that cosmic gas prior to reionisation is mostly cold, while at later epochs the warm phase becomes dominant due to enhanced star formation activity and increasing UV reionising radiation. Stellar return fractions at these times are ~0.15-0.20, a factor of two lower than the values usually adopted. Cold, warm, and hot gas masses as well as HI and H2 components show increasing trends with mass and SFR, while depletion times decrease down to 0.01-0.1 Gyr with a weak metallicity dependence. The resulting star formation efficiency remains at the level of a few per cent and gas-to-star fractions decline with mass, influenced by local feedback and environment. Our findings are consistent with ALMA, VLA and IRAM surveys at later epochs, including ALFALFA, xCOLDGASS, GASS, xGASS, EDGE-CALIFA, PHIBBS, and ASPECS. Gas phases are quantitatively related to the underlying stellar populations and can be used to infer unknown quantities. In the appendix we provide fit functions describing the trends of the stellar return fraction, the main sequence, phase mass relations, gas-to-star fractions and depletion times.
item.dc:creator: Umberto Maio, C\'eline P\'eroux
